goal: Measure the strength of an inexpensive, current-evidence text baseline before spending on new recurrent updates. First stage of a deployment feasibility screen, not a method or benchmark-wide comparison.
cases: From the 23 metadata-eligible earlier-event/later-question-session pairs of the first four development users, select two per user in ascending SHA-256 order of 9b-delayed/user/event/question_session. Use the first eligible official changed question and the first eligible other grounded question. All sixteen questions are scored; both are provided only after the index update. A grounded control is associated with a different event, not necessarily an unchanged personal attribute.
service: Index all raw dated user and assistant turns available through the question session, preserving original chronology and timestamps. The old index excludes the actual delayed session. Compare (1) search the old index, (2) add the delayed session once to the old index, then search the corrected index and (3) corrected-index search plus query-matched passages explicitly retrieved from the delayed-session notice. All methods use the exact same lexical search and the same 4-bit generator. Maintain one generated three-message history (two substantive turns) per case. Start from a fresh model cache on the first turn. No gold memory-point text or evidence passed to the service. Frozen four chronological turn chunks per method, with up to 128 document tokens per chunk. No standalone summary of the notice may use the questions. Charge CPU index setup, update, query, tokenization, and full generation, including all per-turn prefixes. Whole-model cache replay and a native correction are outside this first stage.
measurement: Log outputs by numeric event IDs, complete per-event and per-stage times, prompt token counts and number of observed turns. Score the first line using exact normalized aliases and token F1 as descriptive metrics. A shuffled, method-blind, reference-based AI reading will compare semantically equivalent free replies before deciding whether substantive headroom exists. Label the evaluator and preserve errors. Do not report official HaluMem benchmark results or activate paid resources on this screen.
